author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Ashlyn Mercier has returned to patrol duty with the Westborough Police Department after representing Massachusetts in the Miss America competition. Mercier won the Miss Massachusetts title June 20, becoming the first police officer to hold the state crown, and has continued balancing pageant appearances with the demands of local law enforcement.

Mercier joined the Westborough department in 2025 after earning a college degree in national security. She had stepped away from pageant competition the previous year to attend the police academy, then returned after completing that training. Her path places two different forms of public-facing work on the same schedule: emergency response and community outreach.

Her service platform, “Nick’s Courage: One Smile Goes a Mile,” is named for her younger brother Nicholas, a two-time pediatric cancer survivor. The initiative promotes encouragement and support for critically ill children and their families. Back in uniform, Mercier is emphasizing the common ground between her roles: showing up for people during difficult moments, whether through police work in Westborough or appearances connected to her statewide title.
dek: The patrol officer is back at the department after the Miss America competition, continuing two public-service roles centered on community support.
headline: Miss Massachusetts Ashlyn Mercier returns to Westborough police duty
